t.E471.agn: In 2021 EFSA found no safety concern for any use, including infant formula, and did not set a numerical acceptable daily intake; it recommended purity limits for glycidyl esters, 3-MCPD and erucic acid that may remain from production.
t.E471.body: Mono- and diglycerides are split during digestion into glycerol and fatty acids like ordinary fats.
t.E471.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E471.prod: It is an emulsifier produced from vegetable or animal fats by a chemical reaction (esterification).
t.E471.regx.0: Re-evaluated, including for infants; no safety concern, purity limits recommended.
t.E471.summary: One of the most widely used emulsifiers, produced from fats. It improves texture and delays staling in bread, cake, margarine, ice cream and cream-like products.
t.E471.what: It allows oil and water to mix, delays staling and softens texture.
